PullRequest.Title: sessions: add cloud automation API client
PullRequest.Body:

Refs #337478. **Part 1 of a planned PR stack implementing GitHub cloud automations**, rebuilt in small, independently reviewable slices from main. This PR targets main; subsequent PRs will layer discovery/provider integration and UI on top. It does not close or replace #337478 by itself.

### Scope
- Extend the Sessions GitHub API client with Copilot-gateway requests, stable account/session identity and provider/endpoint pinning, timeout/content-type options, pagination and Retry-After metadata, and structured API errors.
- Add the cloud automation API client: repository eligibility, list/detail, create/update/delete, dispatch, recent history, exact-task lookup and abort. Missing detail requests use bounded concurrency (five) and preserve list order.
- Distinguish definite pre-dispatch failures from uncertain mutation outcomes after request-service handoff.
- Add a shared request option to disable browser-to-remote fallback, enabled for Copilot mutations to prevent replay. Existing callers retain the default behavior.
- Add focused transport/client regression tests. Seven files; no provider registration, UI, polling, experiment gate, or automatic cloud requests.

### Review notes
- Requests currently use `https://api.githubcopilot.com/agents/...`, inherited from the full implementation. Earlier authenticated reads succeeded. Tim's API skill documents `https://api.github.com/cmc_internal/api/agents/...`; supported gateway parity and per-route integration-header requirements still need confirmation. The renderer CORS rationale comes from related task APIs, not a completed comparison of both automation routes.
- The three initial CCR findings (remote mutation replay, display-label credential matching, sequential missing-detail requests) are addressed in 4f1ba1a734b with regression tests.
- The browser request-service fixture is suite-scoped to isolate a pre-existing LogService/MultiplexLogger constructor lifecycle issue. Per-test request-path leak checks remain enabled; no logging implementation changes are included.

### Validation
Run from the repository root with Node 24.18.0:
- `npm run transpile-client` — passed.
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\github\test\browser\githubApiClient.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\providers\copilotChatSessions\test\browser\cloudAutomationApiClient.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\services\request\test\browser\requestService.test.ts --reporter dot` — 74 passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `.\node_modules\.bin\eslint.cmd src\vs\base\parts\request\common\request.ts src\vs\sessions\contrib\github\browser\githubApiClient.ts src\vs\sessions\contrib\github\test\browser\githubApiClient.test.ts src\vs\sessions\contrib\providers\copilotChatSessions\browser\cloudAutomationApiClient.ts src\vs\sessions\contrib\providers\copilotChatSessions\test\browser\cloudAutomationApiClient.test.ts src\vs\workbench\services\request\browser\requestService.ts src\vs\workbench\services\request\test\browser\requestService.test.ts` — passed.
- Formatter verification for the same seven files — passed.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed after the CCR fixes.
- Commit hygiene hook — passed for all seven files.
- Changed-line coverage not measured. Latest authenticated end-to-end mutation validation was blocked by invalid authentication; no claim of live CRUD success for this PR.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added call path, missing-prompt response shape, per-page size, concurrency limit, blocking Promise.all, and disabled transport cache are all directly established by changed production code and tests. Only the real-world catalogue size and endpoint latency are uncertain, which affects severity rather than the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Copilot HTTP requests, repeated authentication-session lookups, response parsing, and network connection capacity
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For N summaries lacking prompt, one list invocation performs N additional detail GETs. With concurrency five, critical-path latency grows in approximately ceil(N/5) request-latency waves per page; refreshing repeats the full work because requests are no-store and results are not cached.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased catalogue-load latency, excessive network I/O, lower request throughput, and avoidable API rate-limit consumption
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no cloud-automation catalogue client and therefore no eager per-entry detail traffic; the list endpoint itself supplies the catalogue summaries in one paginated request.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new list implementation maps every automation summary whose optional prompt is absent to get(), eagerly hydrating it through an additional Copilot HTTP request before the page can be appended or the next page fetched.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 116 calls this.get(...) from inside response.data.automations.map(...). The same added method requests up to 100 summaries per page for 10 pages, and the added test explicitly models list responses without prompts and verifies separate detail requests.
Findings.Title: Load catalogue details lazily instead of issuing one GET per summary
Findings.Impact: Opening or refreshing a catalogue with prompt-less summaries waits for one list request plus N detail requests. A 100-entry page requires 20 sequential network waves at concurrency five before list() can proceed, causing visibly slow catalogue loads and avoidable service/rate-limit pressure; the configured 10-page cap permits up to 1,010 requests per refresh.
Findings.Evidence: list() requests per_page=100, then awaits Promise.all over the page. For every entry without prompt, line 116 invokes get(), which performs GET /agents/automations/{id}. The Limiter only caps concurrency at five; it does not reduce call count. GitHubApiClient marks all of these requests disableCache: true, and this client adds no data cache, so each catalogue refresh repeats the fan-out. The tests establish that missing prompts are an intended response shape and that seven summaries produce seven detail requests.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep list() summary-only and call the existing get() endpoint when an automation is opened or edited. If every prompt is truly required for initial rendering, use a server/list response that includes prompts or an explicit bulk endpoint rather than eagerly issuing one detail request per entry.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or refresh a repository's cloud-automation catalogue
Scenarios.CriticalPath: list() must finish every paginated catalogue GET and all prompt-missing detail GETs before returning any definitions. Each page blocks on its detail Promise.all before the next page is requested.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch paginated automation summaries from the Copilot gateway
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One to ten sequential GETs, one per nonempty linked page
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No cloud-automation catalogue request path existed before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Every page request is on the list critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch each prompt-missing automation through the detail endpoint
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: N GETs after grouping; there is no grouping or deduplication, with at most five active at once
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No per-automation detail fan-out existed before this PR; the list endpoint already supplied one summary collection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All N detail responses must complete before list() returns; each page also waits for its details before requesting the next page.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate authentication sessions before each HTTP request
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once for every list and detail request, therefore 1 + N per page in the prompt-missing case
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing GitHub requests already performed one lookup per request, but the new catalogue fan-out introduces this multiplicity for catalogue loading.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each lookup precedes and delays its corresponding network dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fallback through the remote-agent request channel after a failed or HTTP 405 browser GET
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per failed list/detail GET; successful local browser requests do not cross this boundary
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: BrowserRequestService already used this fallback; the new Copilot GET path leaves the default enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: When triggered, the remote IPC and remote network request replace the failed local result and remain on the catalogue critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number N of automation summaries whose prompt is absent, up to 100 per page and 1,000 across the hard 10-page cap; there is no deduplication, so effective cardinality is N.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: List pages are serialized. Detail hydration is limited to five concurrent requests, creating ceil(N/5) latency waves per page rather than reducing request count.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: GitHubApiClient sets disableCache/no-store for every request and CloudAutomationApiClient has no positive, negative, or in-flight cache, so warm refreshes repeat all list and detail calls.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed code and tests directly establish prompt-less summaries, N detail calls, five-way limiting, page blocking, and no-store transport behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual catalogue sizes, frequency of prompt omission, and gateway latency are not measured, so the reported issue is medium rather than high severity.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary fan-out: an uncached catalogue refresh performs one detail network request per prompt-less summary and blocks the user-visible load behind five-request waves.

Scenarios.Scenario: Check whether a repository is eligible for cloud automations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: requirePrivateRepository waits for isPrivateRepository's GitHub REST response before allowing the caller to proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate authentication sessions for the selected account
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The cloud-automation eligibility workflow did not exist before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before dispatching the repository GET.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GET repository metadata from GitHub REST
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The privacy result is required before eligibility can be decided.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fallback through the remote-agent request channel if the local browser GET fails or returns 405
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero on local success, otherwise one remote fallback
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This fallback was pre-existing and remains enabled by default.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only triggered after local failure/405 and then supplies the awaited result.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected repository per eligibility check.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One request; no loop, queue, or burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The request is no-store and the client adds no cache, so repeated explicit checks repeat the GET, but cardinality remains one per invocation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the call path and single-request cardinality are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Frequency of eligibility checks is not established, but each invocation is bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the new workflow necessarily performs one bounded metadata read and introduces no multiplicative work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create, update, delete, dispatch, or abort one cloud automation/task
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Authentication lookup, JSON serialization, and one Copilot gateway mutation must complete before the operation resolves. No automatic retry or remote fallback occurs for these non-GET Copilot requests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate authentication sessions and pin the selected account/session
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These cloud-automation mutations did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completes before onDispatch and network handoff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per create, update, run, or abort; delete has no body
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No cloud-automation mutation payload was serialized.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous but bounded by a single user-supplied automation definition before dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send one mutation to the Copilot gateway
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one request per method invocation; no retry or replay
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No cloud-automation mutation network path existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The operation awaits the response or acknowledgement.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One user-requested mutation and its payload; collection size does not affect request count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The client adds no aggregate scheduler, but each method invocation dispatches exactly one request; concurrency is controlled by independent callers rather than a changed loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Mutations bypass browser cache; there is no retry, coalescing, or retained result cache. This is appropriate for non-idempotent/uncertain outcomes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: request count, dispatch placement, timeout, and disabled fallback are directly visible and covered by tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Concurrent invocations depend on future UI/provider callers, which are not included in this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: each mutation is bounded to one network operation, and disabling remote fallback prevents replay and duplicate boundary work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Read one automation, recent run history, or one exact task
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each public method performs authentication followed by one Copilot GET and validates the returned object/collection before returning.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate authentication sessions before the read
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One lookup per API method invocation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These cloud-automation reads did not exist.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GET one definition, up to 50 recent tasks, or one exact task
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The requested data cannot be returned until the response is parsed and validated.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Remote-agent fallback after local browser failure or HTTP 405
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero on local success, otherwise one per failed GET
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The generic browser GET fallback already existed and remains enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: When triggered, it extends the read critical path with remote IPC/network work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One requested automation/task, or at most 50 tasks returned by listRuns.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One request per invocation; no internal fan-out. Multiple caller invocations are not coalesced, but no hot caller is added in this PR.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Requests are no-store and no client cache exists. Repeated caller requests repeat the GET, but this PR adds no polling or automatic caller.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: each method directly issues one request and has no loop.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Future polling frequency is unknown and no polling is added here.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: current methods are bounded single reads; speculative future polling is outside this diff.

Scenarios.Scenario: Existing GitHub REST/GraphQL calls and browser-to-remote fallback
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing callers still perform authentication and one local request, with remote-agent fallback after exception/405 unless explicitly disabled. The new disable flag is only set for non-GET Copilot calls.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing GitHub REST or GraphQL HTTP request
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One local request per invocation, unchanged
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same request and no-store behavior existed before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remains the existing awaited request boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Remote-agent fallback after local exception or HTTP 405
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one fallback per invocation; unchanged for options without disableRemoteFallback
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All requests previously fell back; existing callers still do because the new option defaults to false/undefined.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing call frequency and payload sizes; unchanged by this PR for callers that do not pass accountName.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No limiter, queue, retry, or caller scheduling changes are introduced for existing REST/GraphQL traffic.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing GitHubApiClient requests remain no-store as before. No cache key or lifecycle changes affect existing callers.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the condition explicitly preserves fallback when the optional flag is absent, and tests cover all methods/failure modes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for PR causality; existing traffic cardinality is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: existing callers preserve their prior boundary count and fallback behavior.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review of all seven changed files. One medium-confidence-in-magnitude, high-confidence-in-mechanism boundary-fan-out issue was submitted for eager per-summary catalogue hydration. Other new read and mutation paths are bounded, existing request behavior is preserved by default, and the Copilot 202 early return does not leak an unread transport because the browser request implementation buffers the response before returning.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
